questions.question: Which of the following statements correctly describes the role of a catalyst in a chemical reaction?
options: It slows down the reaction and is completely consumed.
It speeds up the reaction but is chemically changed by the end.
It speeds up the reaction without being used up or chemically changed.
It stops the reaction from happening by absorbing heat.

questions.question: Why can't a single catalyst be used for every chemical reaction?
options: Catalysts are specific to particular reactions, meaning different reactions require different catalysts.
Catalysts can only work in gaseous reactions, not in liquids.
Every catalyst is used up during a reaction and cannot be reused elsewhere.
Catalysts only work if they are mixed with acids first.

questions.question: What are enzymes, and what is their function in living cells?
options: They are biological catalysts that speed up reactions in living cells.
They are non-living minerals that slow down digestion.
They are synthetic polymers that store genetic information.
They are metals that conduct electrical impulses in the brain.

questions.question: In a displacement reaction in solution, what determines which metal will displace another?
options: The metal with the lower melting point will displace the one with the higher melting point.
The metal with the higher density will always displace the lighter metal.
A more reactive metal will displace a less reactive metal from its salt.
A less reactive metal will always displace a more reactive metal.

questions.question: What are the products when magnesium is added to a solution of copper sulfate?
options: Copper hydride and magnesium oxide
Magnesium sulfate solution and copper
Magnesium copper alloy and sulfur dioxide
Copper sulfate crystals and magnesium hydroxide

questions.question: How can displacement reactions be used to investigate metals?
options: To measure the exact boiling point of any given metal.
To turn less valuable metals into gold or platinum.
To confirm the position of a metal in the reactivity series.
To determine the magnetic strength of a transition metal.

questions.question: What is a metal ore?
options: A pure block of metal found deep underground.
A type of rock that contains a metal in a form that can be extracted.
A liquid alloy formed by volcanic activity.
A synthetic material used to coat metal wires.

questions.question: Under what condition can carbon be used to extract a metal from its ore?
options: Only when the metal is more reactive than carbon.
Only when carbon is more reactive than the metal.
Only if the metal ore is completely soluble in water.
Only if the extraction is done at room temperature without heating.

questions.question: Which of the following is a typical set of properties for metals?
options: Brittle, dull, poor thermal conductors, and low melting points.
Soft, soluble in water, and poor electrical conductors.
Strong, shiny, malleable, ductile, and good electrical conductors.
Gaseous at room temperature, highly acidic, and transparent.

questions.question: How do ceramics change during their manufacturing process?
options: They are made from soft substances and become hard and brittle when heated.
They are made from hard metals and become highly flexible when cooled.
They are made from liquid polymers that solidify into elastic sheets.
They are made from gases that condense into soft, gel-like materials.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes an alloy?
options: A pure metal element that has been highly polished.
A mixture of elements that includes at least one metal.
A compound made strictly from non-metal elements.
A geological rock containing unextracted metal ores.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of creating a composite material?
options: To break down a complex material into its individual pure elements.
To combine materials to create a new material with improved properties.
To ensure that the material can dissolve easily in water.
To make a material that is highly reactive with oxygen.

questions.question: How are polymers constructed at the molecular level?
options: From giant metallic lattices held together by free electrons.
From small molecules called monomers that join together to form very long chains.
From individual atoms that remain completely separate and unbonded.
From alternating layers of silicon and oxygen atoms in a crystal grid.

questions.question: What effect does adding a plasticiser have on a polymer?
options: It gets between polymer molecules, allowing them to move over each other more easily.
It creates strong chemical bonds that lock all molecules rigidly in place.
It causes the polymer to dissolve instantly when exposed to air.
It turns the polymer into a highly conductive metal alloy.

questions.question: How do cross-links between polymer molecules affect the physical properties of a polymer?
options: They make the polymer much softer and highly soluble.
They make the polymer harder and less flexible.
They cause the polymer molecules to slide past each other much faster.
They turn the polymer into a gas at room temperature.

questions.question: When a reactive metal reacts with an acid, what are the typical products formed?
options: A metal hydroxide and oxygen gas
A metal oxide and water vapor
A metal salt and hydrogen gas
Pure carbon and nitrogen dioxide

questions.question: What products are obtained when certain highly reactive metals react with water?
options: A metal oxide and chlorine gas
A metal hydroxide and hydrogen gas
A metal carbonate and carbon dioxide
A metal sulfate and oxygen gas

questions.question: What information does the reactivity series for metals provide?
options: It shows how vigorously metals react, compared to each other.
It lists metals in order of their electrical conductivity.
It shows the abundance of different metals in the Earth's crust.
It classifies metals based on their cost and rarity.
